newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Power workers' strike dims Russian Far East.
newsitem.headline: Power workers' strike dims Russian Far East.

text.p: Striking power workers blacked out parts of the Russian Far East on Monday, halving electricity output to protest that they had not been paid for months.
Russian news agencies quoted union leaders as saying that some 16,000 workers were owed millions of dollars in back pay.

"Winter is coming. And if we don't get emergency help from the federal government...then winter is going to freeze the region," Itar-Tass news agency quoted strike leader Gennady Tkachuk, of the power workers' union, as saying.
He said some homes and enterprises would be without electricity for 20 hours a day due to the strike, which started at 8 a.m. on Monday (2100 GMT on Sunday).

Some of the power workers have not been paid since April and on Monday they scorned an offer by regional governor Yevgeny Nazdratenko to resolve the energy crisis within two weeks if the strike was put on hold.
Tass said the governor and federal officials were working to complete a list of emergency measures to resolve the crisis.
Workers blame the governor for a financial crisis at utility Dalenergo, which supplies the Pacific port of Vladivostok, the largest city in the Far East.
Tass quoted the workers as saying the governor had kept electricity rates low to help consumers, but this had brought the company to the brink of bankruptcy.

Many businesses have stopped or delayed payments to the power company, a common problem in Russia where strapped enterprises often put electricity bills -- and workers wages -- at the bottom of their list of payment priorities.
Workers said they were owed 130 billion roubles ($24 million) in back wages.

Separately the governor persuaded regional truck drivers to postpone off their own planned strike, but on Friday several other maritime territory unions threatened to shut down firms across the region on October 10.
Tkachuk said the region would not survive without federal intervention. "Without (federal) intervention, Primore region will not survive the winter."
